- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.3), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to match bearish trend.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.  
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in medium-term (15–30d) horizons; add a small upward bias (0.5–1.5%) if recent price is below 30d moving average.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment >0.5 for 3 consecutive days, raise forecast by 0.5–1.0% of prior 30d mean.  
- Model underperforms when sentiment is mixed (±0.3) — use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day highs/lows to adjust forecast.
